title: Rawframe evidence common definitions, generation 1
description: Shared definitions for ADR-0019 evidence records. This document defines no record of its own and is referenced by every generation-1 evidence schema.

identifier.description: The controlled key and identifier grammar. ASCII only, so canonical JCS member ordering by UTF-16 code unit and by byte are the same ordering.

digest.description: An external content digest. The algorithm prefix is explicit so an unknown algorithm fails closed rather than being guessed from length.

fingerprint.description: An exact identity emitted by an accepted producer. Opaque here: this schema fixes its shape, never its meaning.

safeInteger.description: SPEC-0017's integer subset. No fraction, no exponent, no negative zero, and inside the range both a 64-bit integer and a JSON consumer using IEEE 754 doubles represent exactly.

mediaType.description: The exact media type of an external artifact. The evidence grammar is application/vnd.rawframe.evidence.<kind>.v<generation>+json; other artifacts carry their own registered or vendor type.

descriptor.description: External content identity. A descriptor identifies bytes and is never part of the bytes it identifies, so nothing here may carry its own digest.

attachment.description: A required or diagnostic artifact bound to a record. The storage reference is a hint for retrieval and never an identity: retrieval verifies byte length and digest from the descriptor before use.

attestation.description: What an ADR-0082 trusted_ci claim has to carry so that it can be refuted. Every member is an assertion this schema does not check and rf-evidence verifies offline against the pinned Sigstore trusted root: the bundle descriptor identifies the bytes that were signed, the subject names what those bytes attest to, and the source, workflow, and run members name the producer whose certificate identity must match exactly. The schema's job is to make an unverifiable claim impossible to state; the verifier's job is to refuse a verifiable one that is false.

trust.description: Provenance, not a verdict. The two admitted classes are separated by evidence rather than by assertion: diagnostic_untrusted carries no attestation and may carry none, and trusted_ci must carry the ADR-0082 attestation that makes the claim checkable. That is the rule the earlier const ceiling has been replaced by, and it is stricter than it looks: a record cannot claim trust without also handing over what refutes it, and a claim whose attestation does not verify is a typed failure rather than a quiet demotion.
